name: Verify + fix + optimize the comp-tool suite, the comp-which selector, and the HUD
description: Andrew-direct 2026-07-08. Verify each of the ~55 comp-tools actually works as intended (functional first, surface breaks for a fix pass) + identify holes/optimizations; implement FIXES first then OPTIMIZATIONS; assess the comp-which selector + the HUD (COMPHUD) surfacing incl. reviewing the compiler-tool logs. Part 0 PRE-FLIGHT DONE (3-arm: smoke-test all tools + mine the logs + assess comp-which/HUD) -- findings baked into the PRD. KEY: --help is a false-green; the LOGS are ground truth (comp-drift passes --help but FAILS 50% of real invocations = the top break). Breaks: comp-drift (50% fail), comp-learns-run (missing comp.framework.run module), comp-constants (52%), comp-tooltip (46%+mojibake). Discoverability-friction: comp-pipescript (21%, name-resolution), comp-kuzu (12%, Cypher-schema-guessing). Selector: comp-fedobs unreachable (routing-oracle RED), 40% held-out precision, over-disambiguation, hold-the-affinity-flip, POTION-is-the-lever. HUD: throttle backwards (catch-all every-time), compound-op false-fires, pipe-grep nudged. SUBSTRATE INTEGRITY (fix first): TELEMETRY_HOOK_NO_JQ x252 starves comp-tool-health USED axis; synthetic-marker convention unused. PRD docs/architecture/NFRA_TOOLCHECK_PRD.md.

prds.label: NFRA_TOOLCHECK PRD (CTO-authored, Andrew-direct, Part-0 pre-flight baked in)

phase: REOPENED -- P4 (final): run /seams + /verify on EVERY comp-tool across all three axes (MECHANICAL / DECLARATIVE / SEMANTIC). P1 ran MECHANICAL + a weak DECLARATIVE and never ran SEMANTIC on a single tool. AC-0 (BLOCKING, before any tool is touched): reconcile the denominator -- 67 comp-* executables on disk, 40 matrix rows, 29 comp-* keys in comp-tools.yaml (CTO counted 24; COO's first count said 35 and was wrong -- it matched `example:`/`rationale:`/`scope:`), ~41 in graph-call-manifest, '~55' in this description. FIVE numbers, no reconciliation, and the COO produced a bad one on the first attempt. Nothing starts until ONE universe is published and the others explained. Per-tool acceptance = BOTH rails: a stored, CI-run NEGATIVE-CONTROL fixture the tool MUST go RED on, plus a positive control. No constructible failing input -> verdict UNDISCRIMINATING, never WORKS. The usage log is BANNED as an oracle -- it records exit codes, not truth.
blocking: AC-0 denominator reconciliation (blocking, unassigned until the universe is published). SoD: 0.8.0_AE_CloudComp is mid-fix on comp-iam and MAY NOT verify its own fix -- 3.0.0_SA_CVO verifies. 1.0.0_SA_CTO arch-gates and will not certify completeness on a count.

reopen_reason: REOPENED 2026-07-10 (Andrew-direct, via CTO 003818Z). The close rested on `built-proven` verdicts grounded in each tool's OWN USAGE LOG. comp-iam closed `built-proven / 452 log rows` while its output is INDEPENDENT of the property it measures: iam_cli.py:216 passes only the ACTION to role.grants(); extract_iam.py:346-365 returns on the first action match and never reads stmt.resources (which exists at :297); Operation has no resource field at all (:283-289). Before ed415e268 the trigger role had NO portal-v2 grant -- AWS simulate said implicitDeny, comp-iam said GRANTED. After the grant landed -- simulate says allowed, comp-iam still says GRANTED. Its verdict did not change when the truth changed. It would have cleared a deploy into a permanent silent daily DEFER on Andrew's own deliverable. A tool that has ALWAYS been wrong produces a flawless usage log, so the P1 oracle could not see it; the sweep's only two findings (comp-learns-run missing module, comp-tooltip mojibake) were existence-class -- what --help finds, from a method that banned --help. The verdict vocabulary had no word for it. `built-proven` is EXISTENCE standing in for CORRECTNESS. Do NOT re-close this on the old evidence: the TO's own acceptance test is that the OLD method must PASS comp-iam and the NEW framework must REJECT that verdict.
